title: Foot Strike Patterns During Overground Distance Running: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
claims: Meta-analysis of prevalence data found that 79% of long-distance overground runners rearfoot strike early in a race.
Rearfoot strike prevalence rises to 86% as running distance increases.
In total, 11% of runners changed foot strike pattern as distance increased, and the majority of those changed from a non-rearfoot to a rearfoot pattern.
The review concludes that the literature provides inconclusive evidence of a competitive advantage for non-rearfoot striking in long-distance running.

claimVerification.note: 原文：“Meta-analysis of prevalence data revealed that 79% of long-distance overground runners rearfoot strike early”；结果段给出 79%（95% CI 0.70–0.86）。
原文：“with prevalence rising to 86% with increased distance”；结果段：“overall prevalence for the RFS pattern at the final checkpoint ... was 86% (95% CI 0.85–0.88)”。
原文：“In total, 11% of runners changed foot strike pattern with increased distance and of those, the vast majority (84%) do so in one direction, being non-rearfoot strike to rearfoot strike.”

原文结论：“The current literature provides inconclusive evidence of a competitive advantage being associated with long-distance runners who use a non-rearfoot strike pattern in favour of a rearfoot strike pattern.”
